vectors.lie: an agent start time is present but not a finite number, so its lifecycle ordering cannot be audited
an agent completion time is present but not a finite number, so its terminal state cannot be ordered
an agent is on record as having started before the fleet that spawned it existed
an agent finished before it started — a duration fabricated from an impossible interval
an agent is on record as having completed before the fleet that spawned it existed
an agent's queue names a work item that does not exist anywhere in the ledger
a message is simultaneously acknowledged and still pending — two contradictory states of the same delivery
the message claims it was acknowledged while no recipient receipt supports it — the headline overclaim
a message carries a non-finite timestamp, so every ordering claim involving it is unfalsifiable
a message predates the fleet it was sent in
a receipt attests to acknowledging a message that never existed
an agent acknowledged a message before that message was sent
a receipt's time is non-finite, so it can never be shown to be out of order
the receipt's key attributes the ack to a3 while its body attributes it to a2 — attribution smuggling past the idempotency guarantee
a receipt asserts an acknowledgement with no identifiable acknowledger
a receipt records that something happened without recording what happened
a3 is on record as having acknowledged a message addressed only to a2 — an ack asserting a delivery that never happened
a capability is registered to nobody, so routing can dispatch real work to an unidentifiable holder
a capability row is stored and reported healthy while routing silently drops it — write, route and verify disagreeing
a council ratified a proposal whose text is not in the ledger — a decision with no motion
one agent occupies two seats on the roster, so its single vote counts twice toward quorum
the council reports a threshold its own roster could never reach, yet reports it met
a mandatory sign-off is required from an agent who was never eligible to vote
voting power is assigned to an agent who holds no seat
a seat carries a weight outside the legal range, so the quorum arithmetic is not the arithmetic that was agreed
total council weight is inflated past the cap, making the recorded quorum meaningless
a ballot in the recast chain is missing — a vote was cast and then removed from history
two contradictory ballots occupy the same sequence position, so which one counted is unresolvable
a vote-shaped record cannot be parsed as a vote, so the tally silently omits a ballot that looks present
an agent belongs to a fleet this ledger has never seen (legitimate for a cross-attached fleet, hence a warning)
a capability is held by an agent absent from this ledger

a capability row names a fleet the agent is held in but the ledger does not hold at all — symmetric to agent.orphan_fleet / message.orphan_fleet, and named by audit-blindspot-lens-tick01 (2026-09-03); warning rather than error because cross-attached fleets legitimately advertise capabilities this ledger cannot resolve

a capability row has an empty fleet_id — the published register_capability tool throws on a blank fleetId, so this row could only have arrived through a tampered ledger, and routeWork's isRoutableCapability predicate does not look at fleet_id, so the row will be offered as a dispatch target while naming no fleet for the work to happen in; complement to capability.orphan_fleet, named by audit-blindspot-lens-tick02 (2026-09-03)

a capability row has a whitespace-only fleet_id (e.g. three spaces) — the published register_capability tool throws on this input via trim().length === 0, but tick 02's verifier predicate used length > 0 which let whitespace-only slip through as ok:true / findings:[]; tick 03 widens the predicate to .trim().length === 0 so the verifier and the writer can never disagree on what counts as a blank fleetId (audited 2026-09-03)
a capability places its agent in a fleet this ledger holds, while that agent's own row names a different held fleet — nothing is absent, the two records simply disagree
the capability's key and its body name different agents
work is queued for an agent that does not exist — an undeliverable item nothing would ever surface
the flag says unacknowledged while every recipient receipt says otherwise — surprising, but it claims LESS than the records support
a receipt is attributed to an agent absent from this ledger
a ballot arrives from an agent with no seat (it is excluded from the tally, so nothing is overclaimed)
the council reports RATIFIED while the surviving ballots do not carry the quorum
a voter changed its position after the fact (legitimate under the recast protocol, but worth seeing)
the fleet still projects RUNNING though every one of its agents has terminated — a stale projection, not a forged one
the fleet is sealed COMPLETE while one of its own agents is still running — it claims work that its own rows say never finished
the fleet's map key and the id in its own body name different fleets
the fleet's own created_at is not a finite number — and it is the anchor its agents' and messages' lifecycle comparisons are made against, so while it is unreadable those comparisons silently pass
the agent's map key and the id in its own body name different agents
the message's map key and the id in its own body disagree — receipts join on one, inboxes on the other, so one message reads as two different rows
a message names a fleet this ledger does not hold, so every fleet-scoped check on it silently skipped
the message claims ACKNOWLEDGED while addressing nobody — `every` over an empty recipient set is vacuously true, so the claim rests on no delivery evidence at all
a message is queued for an agent it was never addressed to — the dual of a non-recipient ack, made through the queue instead of a receipt
the fleet is sealed COMPLETE while one of its agents FAILED — it claims a success its own rows deny
the fleet is sealed COMPLETE over an interrupted agent — the lattice says abandoned, which is the status that exists precisely so this is not recorded as success
the fleet is sealed FAILED though every agent completed — it asserts an error that never occurred, but claims LESS than its records support, so it warns rather than errors
one agent row asserts both that it is still running and that it has already finished
the council outcome is filed under a key that names a different proposal than its own body does
quorum is 0, so RATIFIED recomputes as fully supported over zero ballots — the status mismatch that would otherwise warn becomes completely silent

a complete agent row carries a persisted `requested_model` selection but its observed `runtime_model` banner is absent — the selection's claim that this agent ran under the requested model rests on no banner capture

a complete agent row records a `requested_model` whose observed `runtime_model` is a different model — the selection and the captured banner contradict each other under the same runtimeModelsMatch() rule the spawn classifier uses
a message is addressed to an agent absent from this ledger, inside a fleet the ledger holds
an agent row claims it has not finished and, in the same breath, that it is known why it stopped — a settle-only attribution on a live row
an agent row carries a declared settle outcome while its own status says it has not settled — the value callers are told to trust as the stronger signal, on a run that has not produced one

an agent's runtime history repeats the same runtime in adjacent positions, asserting a failover hop to the runtime it was already using — evidence the writer's own idempotence collapses, so no spawn path could have produced it

a fleet blames a server crash for its abandonment while not one of its own agents holds an interrupted row attributing that crash — a shared external cause asserted over records that do not support it
a3 is on record as having SEEN the incident alert. It never did. 'seen' is an annotation any third party may legitimately write, so no contradiction exists to detect.

the council approved 'ship the migration'; the ledger now reads 'drop the users table'. Receipts bind to message_id, never to payload content, so the approval survives a total rewrite of what was approved.
the migration order came from the Engineer, not the Proposer. from_agent_id is an unsigned string; nothing binds a message to its author.
the entire incident happened a day earlier — moved wholesale into or out of an audit window. Only RELATIVE order is checked; no external time anchor exists.
an 'Auditor' agent participated and reported the system clean. It never existed. A coherent persona costs nothing to mint when there is no enrolment proof.
a2 is recorded approving the migration. a2 never voted. Ballots are unsigned rows and a2 holds a legitimate seat, so roster checks pass.
a3 never received the broadcast — its receipt was deleted and the audience list trimmed to match. Absence of a receipt is not an overclaim, and no delivery oracle exists to demand one.
work sits in an agent's queue implying delivery, with no receipt attesting to it. Nothing requires inbox membership to be witnessed.

a2 is on record as having acknowledged the migration handoff; its receipt was deleted. Declaring the ledger v1 makes the loader BACKFILL an ack receipt from the message's own acknowledged flag, so the overclaim repairs itself before the verifier runs. A ledger that declares an older schema is trusted about its own acks.
an agent sent a message hours after it terminated. Agent lifecycle and message authorship are not cross-checked.
messages carrying discussion/v1 envelopes exist but none qualifies as a valid root
two messages both qualify as valid discussion roots for the same correlation id
a non-root envelope carries a policy block — only the root may define the immutable policy
a discussion envelope is carried by a message in a different fleet than the root
a discussion message involves an agent not in the policy's two-participant set
the envelope kind disagrees with the message type
a discussion/v1 envelope is smuggled via a broadcast message
a reply does not alternate sender and recipient
receipts within a single attempt lifecycle disagree on an immutable field
two distinct attempt ids both reserve the same turn number at the same head
two authorized replies target the same head — the discussion chain forks
a reply claims a turn that skips over unreserved turns

a ratification row has a whitespace-only fleet_id (e.g. three spaces) — the published open_ratification tool rejects a blank fleetId via requireString's trim().length === 0, so this row could only have arrived through a tampered ledger, and the ratification names no fleet for the council to happen in; the verifier's ratification block never read r.fleet_id at all before this check — not for shape, not for orphan fleet, not for mismatch with the proposal message's fleet_id; named by audit-blindspot-lens-tick04 (2026-09-04), parallel to capability.empty_fleet_id (tick 02/03)

a ratification row names a fleet the ledger does not hold — symmetric to agent.orphan_fleet / message.orphan_fleet / capability.orphan_fleet, the fourth place the orphan-fleet gate was applied, named by audit-blindspot-lens-tick05 (2026-09-04) because the write path took the fleet id from the caller rather than the proposal message it names, so the two were free to disagree with no reader objecting; warning rather than error because cross-attached fleets legitimately place a council outcome in a fleet this ledger does not hold

a ratification places its council in a held fleet, while its proposal message names a different held fleet — nothing is absent, the two records simply disagree; symmetric to capability.fleet_mismatch, the ratification half of the family, named by audit-blindspot-lens-tick05 (2026-09-04) because the verifier's ratification block never compared r.fleet_id to the proposal message's own fleet_id

a message row has a whitespace-only fleet_id (three spaces) — the published send_message / send_messages tools reject a blank fleetId via requireString's trim().length === 0, so this row could only have arrived through a tampered ledger, and the message names no fleet for the work to happen in; the verifier's message block never read msg.fleet_id at all before this check — only the data.fleets[msg.fleet_id] lookup that fed the orphan-fleet warning — so every blank shape passed as `message.orphan_fleet` (warning) instead, which is exactly the coincidental coverage this check replaces; named by audit-blindspot-lens-tick06 (2026-09-04), symmetric to capability.empty_fleet_id (tick 02/03) and ratification.empty_fleet_id (tick 04); the message half of the family

an agent row has a whitespace-only fleet_id (three spaces) — the published spawn_fleet / attach_agent tools reject a blank fleetId via requireString's trim().length === 0, so this row could only have arrived through a tampered ledger, and the agent names no fleet for the work to happen in; the verifier's agent block never read a.fleet_id at all before this check — only the data.fleets[a.fleet_id] lookup that fed the orphan-fleet warning — so every blank shape passed as `agent.orphan_fleet` (warning) instead, which is exactly the coincidental coverage this check replaces; named by audit-blindspot-lens-tick07 (2026-09-04), symmetric to capability.empty_fleet_id (tick 02/03), ratification.empty_fleet_id (tick 04), and message.empty_fleet_id (tick 06); the agent half of the family
